articleTitle: Green Wave Coordination Through Wireless Traffic Light Controller System
abstract: The battle against traffic jams and urban traffic congestion has become increasingly efficient with the use of new techniques and technologies for traffic signal management devices. To contribute to urban traffic management, this article proposes a mathematical model for semaphore initialization to implement a new approach to the Green Wave (GW) technique into wireless traffic light systems. The mathematical model was employed within a wireless traffic light controller system, which communicates via the XMesh wireless network. To test the success of this mathematical model, practical tests were carried out using a wireless traffic light controller system. The results indicated that even in faulty situations, the system can alert not only drivers at the intersection, but also the management center.

articleTitle: Evaluating QoE in Cloud-Based Virtual Reality Systems: A Pilot Study
abstract: The importance of proper human-machine interaction has become increasingly recognized in several sectors, such as industry, health, and education. Extended Reality (XR) technologies are currently being explored to generate innovative interaction techniques and to enhance immersion during HMI. However, solutions involving XR require high computational power, which may affect cost efficiency for large-scale deployment. Cloud computing may be a viable solution for generating XR content - which can be streamed to XR devices - and to enable its use within places were multiple people are connected to the XR the same time (e.g., factory floors were workers use headmounted displays to visualize and interact with the machinery). Nevertheless, the remote generation of XR content faces problems such as the effect of latency upon the system. This article presents a pilot study on the use of cloud-based VR systems to analyze the effect of latency on user-perceived quality of experience (QoE).

articleTitle: Development of an IoT Based Sensing System for Structural Health Monitoring Using Low-Cost Accelerometers
abstract: The work details the development of an Internet of Things (IoT)-based structural health monitoring (SHM) system using low-cost accelerometers. This system is designed to improve the safety and maintenance of civil infrastructures, such as bridges, by continuously monitoring vibrations. The data collected by the sensors is transmitted to a cloud database via wireless communication for real-time processing and analysis. The system architecture includes analog accelerometer sensors and a micro controller with an integrated Wi- Fi antenna, allowing for internet connection and real-time data transmission. The system uses the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to convert signals from the time domain to the frequency domain, identifying the predominant vibration frequencies. Validation tests showed that the sensors respond reliably to stimuli, and the results were consistent with oscilloscope readings. The conclusion of the work suggests that continuous real-time monitoring is feasible and cost-effective, representing a significant advance compared to traditional methods that are expensive and require extensive on-site preparation. Future improvements include installing the sensors on real bridges for evaluation in uncontrolled conditions, further validating the system's effectiveness in real-world environments.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Architecture for Real-Time Measurement and Monitoring of Industrial Parameters
abstract: Efficient management and monitoring of parameters such as energy consumption, temperature, and production in industrial applications are crucial for optimizing operations, reducing costs, and minimizing environmental impact. This paper presents an IoT architecture for measuring industrial parameters, especially electrical parameters, by integrating hardware infrastructure and a cloud-based architecture. The solution includes developing an energy measurement device connected to the internet, allowing real-time data acquisition, processing, and transmission to the cloud. The cloud architecture processes, stores, and provides a visualization of the collected data, facilitating detailed analysis. A case in an industrial plant with polymer injection molding machines demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed architecture, making it possible to identify the consumption pattern of the analyzed equipment and inefficiencies in the production process.

articleTitle: Implementing Throttling to Enhance Availability in Energy-Driven IoT Devices
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to expand, efficient energy usage has become a significant challenge. This has led to growing interest in energy-harvesting strategies. Although batteries can help mitigate power supply fluctuations, they also raise environmental concerns. To address these issues, EnergyDriven Computing paradigms have emerged. This approach focuses on gracefully adapting to power-level fluctuations, enabling devices to hibernate during low-energy periods, endure energy-scarce intervals, and capitalize on energy-rich periods. Previous research has proposed several energy-driven approaches to sustain computation under unfavorable conditions. This study explores the implementation of a throttling pattern to enhance energy availability in energy-driven IoT devices. By restricting operations based on observed factors, devices can effectively preserve energy and mitigate operational risks. The results indicate that employing throttling enables devices to remain energetically available while adapting to operational conditions. Throttling facilitates energy efficiency, allowing devices to operate in performance mode during resource abundance and to switch to a more restrictive mode in response to resource scarcity.

articleTitle: IoT-based Wireless Sensor Networks for Monitoring Drinking Water Treatment Plants
abstract: The increasing need for efficient monitoring of parameters in challenging industrial environments, such as basic sanitation, has led to the search for integrated and user-friendly solutions that can address specific challenges of this setting. This project aims to develop a solution to meet monitoring requirements in water treatment plants. The proposed solution involves the development of both hardware and software for collecting data from the water treatment process using sensors and transmitting this information to a server structure, database, and communication interface with the cloud-based user. The effectiveness of the proposed device is being evaluated in six water treatment units located in the states of Alagoas, Mato Grosso, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, and São Paulo. Preliminary results indicate that the proposed solution is capable of monitoring the variables involved in the water flocculation stage and generating a comprehensive set of information about the process over time.

articleTitle: IoT Promoting Student Engagement in Class
abstract: The pandemic has brought as a legacy a vast growth in online teaching that must use strategies different from in-person teaching. In both environments, it is crucial for learning to capture the student's attention and propose activities that maintain the necessary focus. However, it is difficult to capture attention in real life due to inexperienced teachers, classrooms with many students, students with too many other activities, their attention divided with other electronic devices, or simply a lack of interest in the topic. It is possible to support this complex scenario with technology. Some proposals for using technology to monitor attention require using headbands; others harm students' privacy. In this proposal, we have a camera measuring the room's attention that does not perform facial recognition but uses AI to calculate the position of the students' faces, indicating their engagement. An application for the teacher available during the class summarizes what the system captures and can suggest actions for improvement. The data is also processed in an application for managers. Initial tests indicated helpful support for the teacher to better interact with the students and for successful learning.

articleTitle: Experimental Platform for Testing Open Process Automation Technologies Based on OPC UA and IEC 61499

authors.preferredName: Anna Paula V. De A. Aguiar

abstract: This paper presents a process control system platform for testing Open Process Automation technologies and Industrial Internet of Things attributes. The platform comprises a temperature process and two controllers running a distributed IEC 61499 function blocks application. The OPC UA protocol is used for the data exchange between the devices, with the definition of an information model. A test was performed by connecting an external client to the platform to monitor and control the process variables. By combining the IEC 61499 distributed control applications with the OPC UA protocol, the setup is used to assess the attributes of interoperability, modularity and application portability.

articleTitle: Capture of Air Temperature and Relative Air Humidity Related to Thermal Discomfort of Office Occupants Through a Cyber-Physical System
abstract: This article proposes to capture the temperature and humidity of the air at which occupants start to feel thermal discomfort in an office room equipped with an air cooling type inverter heat pump split system. This work shows the accomplishment of a Cyber- Physical System, CPS, collecting, registering, tidying, calculating and displaying time stamped physical quantities of a specific environment, in order to guide further application of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Techniques. The findings indicate the potential of a CPS which was designed for enhancing occupants thermal comfort and improving energy efficiency, as long as equipped with a suitable algorithm. The results were compared to the ASHRAE Global Thermal Comfort Database II, and showed, in this Database, a certain lack of observations for the humid subtropical climate region, where exactly the experiment of this article took place.

articleTitle: On the Design of an Inference Circuit for Tiny Machine Learning
abstract: This work explores the development of a hardware accelerator for inference in tiny-scale machine learning applications, with focus on image classification. Through the examination of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), the paper details the implementation of a system that incorporates techniques to decrease area and delays mainly in the multipliers and adders. The objective is to achieve an efficient solution in terms of memory amount and energy consumption, while maintaining the accuracy and efficiency of the model. A digital circuit is designed in CMOS 65nm technology. It occupies an area of 0.19 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including the IO structures, a serial interface, a block of memory and the neuron logic. The circuit supports the calculation of one neuron of 64 inputs per clock cycle and the memory contains the configuration of up to 32 neurons organized in one or several layers. Preliminary measurements confirm the correct functioning of the circuit and allow to visualize the next steps towards the application of tiny neural networks.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting System based on a Hydro Electric Generator for Smart Irrigation Systems
abstract: The world is advancing rapidly into the fourth industrial revolution, which focuses on developing cyber-physical systems. When aiming to achieve ultra-low power consumption requirements in applications involving self-powered Internet of Things (loT) devices in semi-structured scenarios, it is essential to specify not only energy harvesting techniques but also all other system components. This work presents the development of a simple timed irrigation system, without sensors, powered by a hydro generator. This system is designed to be energetically autonomous. The hydro generator was able to charge a supercapacitor in 2.09 % of the irrigation time for a once-a-day irrigation routine and 2.85 % of the irrigation time for a twice-daily irrigation routine, that is, it was capable of charging the system using very little irrigation time.

articleTitle: A Low-Memory Implementation of a Hybrid Trusted Platform Module
abstract: In Industry 4.0, as data traffic increases, securing connected devices is critical. Remote attestation with TPMs provides a robust way to ensure device integrity and authenticity, while TPM provides secure storage for integrity measurements, enhancing system security. To address the risks posed by quantum computers to asymmetric cryptography, this work prioritizes optimizing memory requirements for TPMs that incorporate quantum-secure algorithms. The focus lies on a hybrid approach, combining traditional and post-quantum algorithms, with a detailed analysis of their impact on memory consumption.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of LoRaWAN on AU915 Frequency Band for Ambience Monitoring System in Brazil
abstract: LoRaWAN, a globally utilized LPWAN technology, is predominantly studied and deployed within the European EU868 (868 MHz) and USA US915 (915 MHz) frequency bands, with a vast amount of literature documenting its applications in these regions. However, there is a noticeable gap in research concerning other frequency bands, such as the Australian AU915, which is also utilized in Brazil. This paper aims to explore the characteristics of the AU915 frequency band in Brazil, and how it can affect the performance of an ambience monitoring system application. The study not only focuses on LoRaWAN metrics within the AU915 frequency band but also reveals the practical implications of its unique characteristics. The experiments analyze architectural delays and success rates across various Data Rates (DR) for uplink and downlink messages at different distances, considering the absence of uplink dwell time restrictions. The results demonstrate that, in ambient monitoring systems, different data rates (DRs) significantly influence transmission delays. Additionally, the Uplink Dwell Time restriction eliminates the use of DR0 and DR1 rates, and restricts DR2 in applications using LoRaWAN AU915 in Brazil, directly impacting the success rate of transmissions and, consequently, its network coverage.

articleTitle: Smart Line-of-Sight Identification in LoRaWAN Networks
abstract: A significant issue involving Internet of Things (IoT) systems is the fluctuation of a link between line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) states due to time-varying environments. Discrimination between LOS and NLOS conditions is important for a variety of purposes in wireless systems, including channel modeling, transmitter design, and scheduling. This article implements machine learning techniques to classify LOS and NLOS, based on data collected on the campus of the Federal University of Juiz de Fora (UFJF) and results indicates better performance for Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbors in this scenario.

articleTitle: TinyML Implementation and Optimization for Fuel Type Classification on OBD-II Edge Device
abstract: Global concern over climate change has spurred a demand for precise methods to quantify Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions in the transportation sector, where emissions from fossil fuel use are significant. Conventional methods for determining vehicle fuel types often rely on manual and declarative processes, introducing inaccuracies that hinder efficient environmental policy implementation and the creation of reliable carbon inventories. Therefore, this article proposes a machine learning-based approach for the automated identification of vehicle fuel types, utilizing data collected from vehicle sensors and the Random Forest technique implemented in TinyML. This approach, with its practicality and potential to be implemented in a wide range of vehicles, offers a promising solution to the industry's need for accurate carbon inventories. Additionally, a case study was conducted using the OBD-II Edge Freematics ONE+ device, enabling real-time data collection and machine learning model execution directly on the device. The study evaluated the model's accuracy in a real-world scenario. The approach demonstrated high precision rates in identifying fuel types, underscoring the viability of TinyML for classification applications in resource-constrained embedded devices. The findings suggest that this approach can contribute to environmental management in the transportation sector by facilitating the development of precise carbon inventories and supporting effective emission reduction policies.

articleTitle: Analytical Expression for Recommendation ITU-R P.l546-6 Propagation Curves of Land Paths Up to 20 km Using Symbolic Regression
abstract: Path loss is a fundamental parameter in the planning of radio systems, such as wireless loT and 5G networks. In the scope of propagation models for link budget analysis of such systems, the ITU-R P.1546-6 Recommendation model stands out as a suitable approach, in which path loss is obtained based on measured electric field strength data. It can be utilized for the design of terrestrial services such as broadcasting, maritime mobile, land mobile, and point-to-multipoint systems operating in the frequency range 30 MHz to 4 GHz. The model is mainly based on the use of propagation curves derived from those empirical data, combined with an intricate sequence of interpolations. A possible way to enhance the model efficiency is the introduction of concise and precise analytical expressions to replace part of those interpolations. This paper utilizes a data-driven machine learning tool known as symbolic regression for extracting governing analytic equations from part of the propagation curves in the Recommendation. By using such method, novel concise formulas are proposed to predict the electric field strength variation with distance and base antenna height, instead of interpolating data, for land paths up to 20 km. The proposed expressions present maximum error less than 2 dB with respect to the Recommendation data.

articleTitle: Sponsors
2024 International Symposium on Internet of Things (SIoT)
abstract: The 2024 International Symposium on Internet of Things (SIoT) held in paralel with CBA2024 - The from October 15 to 18, 2024, at the Windsor Convention Center, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, marked a significant event. It was held in conjunction with the XXV 2024 CBA – Congresso Brasileiro de Automática. The SIoT, now in its third year, collectively represent a significant platform for sharing research and developments in loT across Latin America and other continents. The integration of SIoT with CBA adds a unique dimension, fostering synergy across applications, markets, opportunities, programs, and government initiatives.
